compiled_state.description:
Store the baseline in the projection the comparison already computes: `description` as
`normalize_rich_text(raw)`, `status`/`priority` as `.name`. Expected ~-66% on an **18.3 MB**
(18,257,550-byte) file. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why this is safe without a comparator change
`outbound_field_diff.py:187,196` canonicalize BOTH sides at **read** time via
`inbound_mapper.map_remote_to_local` (docstring `:183`: "storage stays vendor-shaped, mapped at READ
time only"), and both canonicalizers are idempotent on already-normalized values:
`normalize_rich_text` (`inbound_fields.py:136-145`) returns `adf_to_text(body)` for dicts and
`str(body)` otherwise; `_extract_jira_field_value` (`:92-96`) reads `name`/`displayName` for dicts and
passes strings through. So ADF-dict and plain-text baselines canonicalize identically and a mixed
store needs no new comparator. This also makes the change **revert-safe** — a normalized-string
baseline round-trips unchanged through pre-A3 code.

CORRECTION carried forward: an earlier framing rested on `_extract_jira_field`/`_diff_fields`, which
have **zero production callers**. Validate against the live path only.

## Why assignee is EXCLUDED — data loss, not conflict noise
`_assignee_candidates` (`outbound_field_diff.py:56-67`) builds its match set from the scalar **plus
every non-None identity form**, and `_suppressed_by_inbound` (`:250-256`) routes assignee through
`_assignee_matches`. Collapsing three identity forms to one string shrinks that candidate set and
loses inbound-directionality suppression, so local-wins **silently clobbers a concurrent remote
assignee edit**. (The strict `assignee_identity` equality at `:390-394` is the lesser, secondary
effect.) Keep assignee raw.

## Trap to pin
Store exactly `normalize_rich_text(raw)` — any other text extraction (fit/truncate/strip variants)
diverges from what the same ADF decodes to on the read path and fabricates a permanent diff.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A **dict-shaped** baseline fed through the live `compute_update_fields` path yields the **same
      verdict** as its normalized-string equivalent. Tier: **integration** through the real
      production comparison path. **This test does not exist today** —
      `test_binding_baseline.py:36-59` and `test_baseline_arbitration.py:91` use flat strings only, so
      a no-op-on-strings normalizer would leave them green while proving nothing. This is the RED case.
- [ ] The direction-preservation suite, extended with assignee shape cases (email / accountId /
      displayName), passes unchanged — proving assignee arbitration is untouched. Tier: **property/unit**.
- [ ] Baseline entries for `description`/`status`/`priority` are scalars after one pass; `assignee`
      remains a dict. Tier: **integration** asserting stored shapes.
- [ ] A corpus diff over real bindings shows **zero mutation delta** before vs after normalization.
      Tier: **repo-level corpus script**.
- [ ] `bindings.json` size drops by >=50%. Verify: byte comparison before/after one full pass.

## Files
`binding_store.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_baseline.py`,
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_baseline_arbitration.py`

Scope: S-M. Depends on A2-1.
